title: Classics
tagline: Read Greece and Rome in their own words, and trace their influence on everything since.
overview:
The Certificate in Classics is a three-year course of study in the languages, literature, history, and culture of ancient Greece and Rome. You begin with the classical world and its myths, start Latin and ancient Greek in your first year, and read Homer and Greek drama alongside the history of Greece and Rome.

The core takes you through intermediate Latin and Greek prose and poetry, philosophy, epic, archaeology, the ancient historians, and the late Roman world. In your final year you choose a concentration in the Greek and Latin languages, ancient history, or classical civilization, and write a senior thesis.
outcomes: Read Latin and ancient Greek texts in the original with the aid of a dictionary and commentary.
Explain the history of the Greek and Roman worlds and the evidence on which it rests.
Interpret classical literature, philosophy, and art in their cultural contexts.
Use textual, material, and documentary sources critically.
Trace the reception of classical culture in later periods.
Conduct and present original research in classics.
